messages:
maria: finished initial onboard for mercator-v2 int8 — short-query recall@10 looks off, raising a flag.
aj: can you paste the numbers real quick?
maria: quick summary: fp16 baseline recall@10: 0.886. int8 (per-channel symmetric) recall@10: 0.820. delta ~ -0.066 absolute (~7.4% relative).
sophia: that's bigger than i'd expect for per-channel. which calibration / clipping did you use?
maria: default dynamic range + no explicit clipping. command I ran: ```python
run_eval(model='mercator-v2', quant='int8_per_channel', dataset='short-queries', k=10)
```
eval-bot: eval-bot: median latency 3.2ms (fp16 baseline 2.8ms). embedding cosine mean-shift: 0.023.
kev: did you look at cluster metrics (silhouette / purity)?
maria: silhouette avg dropped 0.12 -> 0.05. small clusters show centroid drift and higher intra-cluster cosine variance. (plot not attached here).
aj: can you break recall down by query length bins? 1-5 / 6-20 / 21+ tokens
maria: ran that quickly: bins results (fp16 -> int8): 1-5: 0.78 -> 0.61 ; 6-20: 0.88 -> 0.85 ; 21+: 0.91 -> 0.90. short queries take the lion's share of the regression.
sophia: sounds like low-norm / low-magnitude vectors are getting crushed into quant bins. try KL calibration + asymmetric quant, or clip at 0.995 quantile. also test per-channel with different block sizes.
maria: will try asymmetric per-channel + KL clipping. plan: run mercator-int8-kl-clip and also a per-tensor baseline for comparison on the same holdout (100k).
aj: also check nearest-neighbor angular distribution — if you see many ties at top-k that's consistent with recall drop. maybe add tiny gaussian noise during quantization as a test.
maria: noted. current reconstruction pipeline used: ```python
emb = model.encode(batch)
q = quantize_per_channel(emb)
rec = dequantize(q)
rec = rec / np.linalg.norm(rec, axis=1, keepdims=True)
```
I suspect normalization after reconstruction amplifies small quant errors.
eval-bot: eval-bot: queued run mercator-int8-kl-clip -> expected finish ~15m (job id ejb-2319).
kev: FYI I bumped staging batch_size to 128 to better match production throughput and catch any micro-batching artifacts.
sophia: if KL fix reduces short-query delta under ~3% we can accept int8 broadly and put a short-query fallback to fp16. otherwise we need more aggressive scheme (mixed precision routing).
maria: agreed. i'll post the KL run results and per-length recall table once eval-bot finishes. cc @aj
